correctness.rationale: For every m>=4 the semigroup is closed since two positive members sum to at least 2m. Normalized ideals are S plus selected gaps. Their dual is calculated exactly from the positions in the middle block forbidden by selected small gaps. All high gaps are in any nontrivial bidual and all negative integers are excluded by t=2m-1-x. Thus bidual fixed points reduce to a complete edge/endpoint cover of the path of length m-2, equivalent to avoiding isolated interior selected vertices (the substring 010). This reconstructs the claimed unique parametrization. Last-symbol recurrence proves the generating function; counting forced high gaps gives all-ideal count; a concrete N5 interval proves the nonmodular threshold. Direct code checks 4,133 normalized ideals, m=4,...,12, but infinite proof is textual.

value.rationale: Divisorial closure is an intrinsic fractional-ideal invariant. The claim classifies every translation class of its fixed points for an arbitrarily large near-ordinary semigroup family, identifies their exact inclusion lattice, computes a nontrivial cubic enumeration and exponentially small fraction among all ideals, and proves a sharp onset of lattice nonmodularity. The family is a canonical minimal two-high-gap deformation, not an arbitrary finite slice. These results go beyond applying a general colon formula to a single ideal; they supply reusable structure and exact infinite-family counts.
